analysis.title: Softer US core CPI, finally?
key_insights: CACIB expects October US core CPI at 0.26% MoM SA, 2bp above the 0.24% Bloomberg consensus average. It compares with 0.29% in August (boosted by noise in telephone services) and 0.33% in September.

Headline US CPI is forecast at 0.29% MoM SA for October. No YoY figure can be calculated because the BLS never published the October 2025 index after last year's government shutdown, so there is no YoY consensus either.
The 3M moving average of core CPI, annualised, would come out at 3.53% in October, the highest since January 2025. CACIB expects a relatively benign report with core back around 0.25% MoM.
After the recent sharp drop in Brent crude, CACIB's model puts headline CPI at about 3.5-3.6% YoY until February 2027. The peak was 4.25% YoY in May 2026.
CACIB does not expect a major CPI impact from the blue wave result of the midterm elections, beyond the lower crude prices already in its model.

Second-round effects from higher energy prices (Iran war) in core are very limited so far, apart from airfares (1.3% of the core CPI basket). Some pass-through has started in core goods but is not significant yet.

Last year's tariffs are leaving the YoY calculation, which lowers core goods CPI YoY. OER and rent YoY will be abnormally strong from November 2026 to March 2027 because of the BLS's methodology choices after the 2025 shutdown.
CACIB sees core CPI around 2.5% YoY at an end-2027 horizon. Base effects (tariffs, statistical treatment of OER and rents) will dominate YoY readings through late 2026 and early 2027.

Even with the forecast, the October report would still be firmer than ideal for the Fed. CACIB expects a 25bp hike in December and a final 25bp hike in March, 75bp in total, reversing last year's insurance cuts at an every-other-meeting pace before another pause.
Last Friday's payrolls report surprised strongly to the upside at +165k against a consensus of +70k.

tension_points.bull_case: October core CPI is forecast at 0.26% MoM, softer than August (0.29%) and September (0.33%). Tariffs are leaving the YoY calculation, pulling core goods lower, and crude has dropped sharply.
tension_points.bear_case: The 3M annualised core rate would still be 3.53%, the highest since January 2025. OER and rent YoY will be abnormally strong from November 2026 to March 2027 because of the BLS methodology, and the report would still be firmer than ideal for the Fed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core print meaningfully above 0.26% MoM (Bloomberg consensus is 0.24%) would undercut the softer-inflation view.
